utterances.text: Did your municipality ever take a decision to reduce the number of Muslims and Croats in the municipality to the extent required for the Serbian authorities to function?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you learn, see or hear that any other body in the RS took such a position?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I was unaware of that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And had you heard what President Tudjman was saying about the acceptable percentage of Serbs in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: That was the period before the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Unfortunately, many statements were made that could be called warmongering statements that threatened the Serbian population. And when I said that from Croatia between 6- and 7.000 refugees of Serbian ethnicity had come from Croatia to my municipality, I believe that's very telling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For planning purposes, the Chamber wants to know how much longer would you need?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably until the end of this session, your Excellency, possibly less. Maybe 20 minutes will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will rise for five minutes. --- Break taken at 2.11 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the remainder of this session, we'll be sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis with Judge Morrison being away due to his urgent personal matters. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that you attended some meetings of the regional or provincial level. Were those -- or, rather, did those meetings include the time, place, and the participants, more or less?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. Mostly they did. However, that was not regulated in any way. So if we speak about regional meetings, they mostly took place in Banja Luka. Some deputies assembled there. Actually, I think it depended on your position, if you were the president of the municipality or the Executive Council or -- and so on. It's mostly those people who went.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see P2641.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, in Vukelic's text and in the document with the annexed signatures, it says that it took place on the 8th of June. Can you tell us if this is the same meeting dated the 7th of June here? Is this sheet of paper satisfactory with regard to the formal elements? What shall it contain? What shall it include?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: This format is unknown to me I can say, because the lawyers there had a certain practice. There would be a heading, including the date and certain preamble and only then would conclusions follow. So I'm not sure that this is authentic based on the format, although I have nothing specific that I can -- no specific arguments to doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can I interrupt? I think Mr. Karadzic may be confusing the witness. He's -- he refers to P2641, which is the conclusions of Sanski Most on the 7th of June and then refers to Vukelic's text, which is the 9th of June, and the document with the annexed signatures which as we know is the 14th of June and says that it took place on the 8th of June here. What took place on the 8th of June was the ARK Crisis Staff meeting, so I'm not sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No. And of course then on -- page 95, line 8 it says the 17th of June. I think that's supposed to read the 7th of June. But they're all different meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I merely wanted us to establish whether this alleged meeting of the 7th of June was the one where they passed -- because you were first shown this one dated the 7th, then the one of the 9th, and finally the one dated the 8th. Were you at two meetings, one of which was at Sanski Most and the other in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Well, all these dates, you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please put a pause. And now could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. Mr. Karadzic is again confusing the record. I didn't show him the ARK Crisis Staff meeting of the 8th. I showed him Mr. Vukelic's report which referred in that to the ARK Crisis Staff meeting the day before, which was the 8th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I wanted to say that all the dates starting with the 1st of June and until the 15th or 16th of June were very difficult days for Bosanski Novi municipality. During that period of time, it was impossible to move around safely. I don't think that I attended all those meetings on the 7th, the 8th, or the 6th, or the 14th -- or, rather, the 7th of June or 14th of June as is claimed. I can't say with any degree of liability that I was there. I don't think I was for technical reasons. I perhaps would have attended if I had been able to move around. I don't know what the outcome of that would have been. However, for technical reasons I couldn't attend those meetings because the situation in Bosanski Novi municipality was difficult, and it was either impossible or barely possible to move around. That was the reason --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now can we look at 65 ter 6737. I believe that the document now has a new number. It is probably 2640. Today it was called up on page 33. Can we see only the Serbian version, and can that version be blown up as much as possible. And can it be scrolled up so as to enable us to see Novi Grad. Could you please read aloud the first sentence under "Bosanski Novi."

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I shall try, although it's not very legible. It says: "In the territory of Bosanski Novi there was an armed conflict between the Green Berets and members of the TO and the police."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us whether there were Muslim paramilitary formations and what were their names? What kind of paramilitaries existed?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Of course they existed. The entire story about the disarming of paramilitary formations testifies to that. However I have to point out that very soon those military -- paramilitaries mutated or, rather, they changed into be civilian clothes. They were most commonly referred to as the Green Berets. They had some other nicknames but that was a common term that they were known as. That's what they styled themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Only page 33 there was an exchange of information and opinions between you and Ms. Sutherland about the presence of heavy calibre weapons. Would you say that the 20-millimetre cannon is a heavy calibre weapon?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: In the former JNA I was a foot soldier. I was a private and I would not provide any professional opinions. However, as a layperson, I would say that this should be a small-calibre weapon. I have reservations about that. I'm not claiming. However, I am following my own logic when I say that it is a small calibre weapon. There were mortars. I believe that there were 60- and 80-millimetre mortars and that in the then establishment of the former JNA this was all considered light artillery or infantry weaponry. I don't know exactly what those things were called but I'm not an expert. I will admit that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we see P3842.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The clash that involved the Green Berets, would you say that the Green Berets were at the same time peasants?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: In formal terms, they shouldn't be. I repeat, those formations according to some information that we had, when they realised they were not a good match to the TO staff in military terms, very soon based on their estimate they hid their uniforms and their weapons. They didn't want to hand those over, and within a very short period of time -- there was a short period of time when they wore military uniforms according to my subjective estimate, but when they realised that they could not be seen as a fair match to the TO, they turned into peasants very quickly, and then you would be right, that peasants also were members of that formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see the second page of that document. You told us here during the cross-examination that you offered members of the UNHCR to go there yourself and to talk with the representatives of the Muslims. Many witness statements were quoted to you or -- and testimonies in the Krajisnik testimony. And the witnesses were recommended by you. The statements as they were represented to you, are they truthful?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: For the most part they are not truthful. All those statements by the witnesses and certain employees of UNPROFOR and the committee on refugees are quite imprecise I would say. It is my feeling that they all tried to attempt telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now see the following page?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness and the accused be reminded to make pauses between answer and answers and speak slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that you offered them to go there on their own and that they did that. Please, were you there on behalf of Bosanski Novi? Did you attend a meeting in Dvor on the 11th of July? It says in the first paragraph: Both sides tried to -- please look at the left-hand side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Can that page be zoomed in a little?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you attend that meeting? Do you know that your representative was there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was on the 11th July. I don't know that for a fact. However, I know that there was a meeting in Dvor at the UNPROFOR base. There were meetings there. In the course of one day we sometimes had even two or three short meetings whenever we reached important -- we received important information. Those meetings were not called in advance. There was no agenda or anything like in peacetime. Some of those meetings were called within the space of a couple of minutes. We would just get together and discuss certain issues and problems. It is possible that I attended that meeting on the 11th. However, I am not sure, I can't say that that was on that day. But I did attend certain meetings in the UNPROFOR base together with the representatives of the commission for refugees from Toposko, representatives of the Muslim people, and myself or somebody else. But in principle I never went alone. There was always somebody with me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness and the accused please be reminded to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's impossible to follow at this speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Speak slowly and utter as few words as possible. Could you please read aloud bullet point 3.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Could it be zoomed in a little.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter doesn't have the English original before her.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the meeting UNHCR crossed the border and went to Bosanski Novi in order to meet with the representatives of the Muslim population which wanted to leave their homes and were getting ready to leave. Despite all explanations, they adhere to their original position that there was no other possibility for them but to leave Bosnia Krajina and go to Croatia, Slovenia, and Western Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this tally with all you know? Was that the moment when you offered them to go and talk to the Muslim representatives themselves without you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether that was the moment or not, but there was a moment or the moment, in any case, when I said to Mr. Jensen or Mr. Jens that he should do that, because he always showed a degree of suspicion about my intentions. So I tried to be as honest as possible and as objective as possible, but I still noticed that they did not trust me, that they did not believe my words, and then I insisted, and I asked them to go there without me. That's when I had realised that they didn't believe me. I didn't want to coerce them into doing anything. I just wanted them to go there and to try and find some of the representatives of the Muslims and talk to them in a very objective way, in an unbiased way. I wanted them to get a true insight into the whole story. I wanted them to get to the bottom of the story and to see whether it was the Serb authorities that they -- if they wanted to throw them out or whether there was a free will of the Muslims to leave. That's why I asked Mr. Jensen to do what I asked him to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, please, did you -- I want to clarify some of the terminology. Did you say or did you imply that they were leaving gladly or that they were leaving of their own free will? Were they rejoicing in the fact that they were leaving or were they sad but still leaving of their own will? It seems to me that it was unnatural for somebody to rejoice and you then said it was an ironic approach. Were they happy? Do you make a distinction between one's own free will and leaving happily?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I do make a distinction. I don't know how the interpreters are going to interpret that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's impossible. Put a pause after Mr. Karadzic asks a question, please wait until the interpretation of the question is interpreted -- is concluded. Now could you answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will repeat. I do make a distinction between happiness and something that is done of one's own freewill. I believe that the degree of euphoria or happiness did not exist on the side of the Muslim population. However, I still claim that there was their own free will to leave the area either temporarily or permanently. This is something that we could discuss. However, they wanted to leave of their own free will. At that moment it was in their best interest. I already told you what their motives to leave Bosanski Novi were, but they did it of their own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 15, I believe that you were -- you were shown P20418 and I would like to recall that document. Could you please tell us which armed forces existed in the municipality and which of them were legal or legitimate?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: May I start answering?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, what it's exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 13, line 23, it says P20418. Maybe the first digit, the first number 2 is surplus. It says P20418, and there's another document 0218 too. The first document should have been a document issued by the ARK on the 4th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, Mr. Pasic, you mentioned earlier today that you wanted the Muslims to get involved in the Territorial Defence. Was the Territorial Defence a legitimate and legal military formation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. Under the Law of the former Socialist Federative Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the former state of Yugoslavia, the Territorial Defence was a legal and legitimate formation and all representatives of all the peoples from the area were its members and the second question, if I may answer that immediately --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a -- I must say a strong desire, on my part at least it did, for the representatives of the Muslim people to become members of legal institutions such always the TO staff, the civilian police, i.e., the SJB, because I personally as a human being believe that if they joined those bodies, if there were Muslims in those bodies that their need for paramilitary formations would diminish and that civilians, regular people, both Muslims and Serbs, would have a security and a guarantee that they would trust bodies with mixed compositions, with membership of Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] and now I would like to call up --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And would Mr. Karadzic repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D9290.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the following page we will see something that has not been translated. Oh, it has been translated. You mentioned joint appearances -- can we go back to page 1. You can see the page where it says joint interest. Can we go back to the first page in the Serbian language, please. You spoke about joint activities involving you and Mr. Izet Muhamedagic. Do you remember these negotiations, and do you remember this press conference and the appeal that was sent from that conference to the citizens in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I'm looking at this text. I'm trying to read it. I'm familiar with the protagonists. These names ring a bell. There were similar statements appealing to the citizens for peace and joint interest, and there were really a lot of them. My role as the president of the Municipal Assembly, i.e., my desire was indeed considerable. Irrespective of the conflicts that had happened before that in Croatia, Slovenia, and then in Bosnia and Herzegovina we wanted us to create an oasis of peace in Bosanski Novi as we called it. Unfortunately, these cries and appeals were futile for the reasons that I've been mentioning throughout my testimony today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I right in thinking that you represented the municipality and that the SDS was represented by Mirko Dejanovic and the SDA was represented by Muhamedagic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, in formal terms I was the president of the Municipal Assembly where MPs were also Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can you look at the last paragraph after where it says "Arms." Everybody can read that it is requested from the Serbs to hand over their illegally obtained weapons but now the last paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Could you please zoom in a bit. That would be a good thing. Which part?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: His Excellency Mr. Kwon thinks it's leading, but if you can read this part.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: "In that sense, Izet Muhamedagic publicly called upon the representatives of the Muslim people who have illegally obtained acquired weapons to hand them over in the way which had already been agreed upon and a similar call was addressed by Mirko Dejanovic to Serbs who illegally possess weapons." Should I go on? "Official authorities and legal armed formations are duty-bound to provide security to citizens who surrender their weapons. Concurrently with the activities on the surrender of weapons, Muslims shall be joining the TO and the public security station for the purpose of creating an ethnic structure that would correspond to the structure of the population of the municipality."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It's on the next page in English. Is that what you spoke of a moment ago, that it would be better if the Muslims had taken part in the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Well, that was the aspiration, to have a single formation in a military and civilian sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3850, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pasic, you were saying that you had difficulties and that it was impossible to do regularly everything that the authorities wanted to do. When did these difficulties of yours start, from when?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Well, unfortunately these difficulties started considerably before the war developments in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I have to point out that the municipality of Bosanski Novi, Novi Grad, had problems already in 1991, already from the month of July, that is to say a year before all these things that we have been speaking about and that this primarily had to do with the Croatia army. It wasn't called the Croatian Army then it was the ZNG and MUP.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D9291, please. Could that be shown to the witness. Thank you. I believe that there is no translation, but I shall present that briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, again Mr. Karadzic put a question to the witness before he brings a document up onto the screen and it's exactly what he did a moment ago with the newspaper article.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've put a question now, too: When did their difficulties start? And this document refers to Mr. Pasic and his information provided to the closest garrison to the effect that there is a war going on on the other side of the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this text says, this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I see that this was sent to the corps, right, of the 1st Military District, to the intelligence organ. I think that's what it says here. So it says that according to my press release it is stated that there is fighting in the area of Hrvatska Kostajnica. That is the area that I was speaking of until now. We even had civilian casualties in that period. The Croatian Army killed civilians in Hrvatska Kostajnica which then belonged to the municipality of Novi Grad Bosanski Novi. It used to be a local commune. So it was only civilian casualties there and I informed the then president of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina about that, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic. On one occasion we spoke on the telephone about that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be adopted for identification, but if we cannot sit longer today, would I like to ask that Mr. Pasic come back tomorrow for about 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That being the case, we will continue tomorrow. I'm told we are running out of tape. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I object to it even being marked for identification. He simply put the document on the screen, told the witness to read it and he has and now he says can the document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll come to this document tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, also, just very briefly, if the tape's running out, I want to tender -- I -- I omitted to tender 06737 in my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which was used by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. And the exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You like it to be admitted as part of Prosecution exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the exhibit that I referred to on transcript page 13 is P02418.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Shall we assign a number for that, 6737.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit P6440, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it okay, Mr. Pasic, to stay over tonight until tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you're asking me what I sincerely think, I wish we could have finished today, but if I should stay until tomorrow, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 10th day of July, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.
